notes:
Account background: Large Tier-1 telco exploring vendor-managed dedicated inference for customer-facing chat + internal reranking. Primary drivers: predictable latency for live chat SLAs, regional failover, and cost predictability for Q3 network launch. Internal sponsors: VP Product (Lian Choi), Head of Infrastructure (Marcus Feld). Procurement lead: Naomi Sato.

Recent timeline / activity (shorthand):
- 2025-11-02: inbound from solutions webinar; AE outreach, qualified.
- 2025-11-10: discovery call - topology, compliance, existing infra (on-prem colo + AWS). Notes: "must keep EU traffic in EU, US west for west customers".
- 2025-12-08: security questionnaire submitted (SSO + KMS emphasized). Drive link shared (montclair-sec-faq).
- 2026-01-12: architecture deep-dive (Fireflies ff-2026-01-12-3321). Discussed dedicated pool sizing, model catalog, and fallback rules. SE attended (Priya).
- 2026-01-20: internal capacity planning workshop; Montclair gave production target: 400 req/s steady-state chat (avg 256 tokens), 99th pct latency target < 300ms, p50 < 90ms.
- 2026-02-03: Redwood proposed draft pool: H100-equivalent reserved pool = 24 GPUs (us-east-1:12, us-west-2:6, eu-west-1:6) with 30% failover headroom; autoscaling burst to shared capacity for extreme spikes.
- 2026-02-14: commercial scoping call - Montclair requests hard throughput guarantees per-region and a defined failover playbook (Fireflies ff-2026-02-14-1107).
- 2026-02-24: Performance POC scheduled (load test scripts & synthetic token distribution agreed). POC window: 2026-03-08 to 2026-03-12 (72h soak + two failover drills).

Technical / requirements summary (shorthand):
- Workloads: real-time chat (low-latency), reranking for query pipelines (high-throughput), occasional bulk embeddings for UX features.
- Latency SLOs desired: p95/p99 < 200-300ms for chat; reranking batch throughput 1-2k qps in region.
- Throughput planning: baseline 400 req/s (256 token avg) per region during peak; want headroom to sustain 2x baseline during failover (i.e., if us-west goes down, us-east must absorb ~800 req/s).
- Reserved pool proposal: 24 GPUs distributed across 3 regions; headroom target = 25-30% reserved above steady-state to cover shipping windows + warm cache.
- Failover design: cross-region shadow routing + prewarmed KV cache trickle; fast fallback to smaller low-cost model variant if sustained overload.
- Cost controls: request for recommendations on batching, quantization (int8/4-bit), and slot preemption policies for predictable unit economics.

Negotiation notes / SLA asks:
- Montclair pushing for uptime SLA 99.95% + latency credits if p99 exceeds threshold more than 3x/month. Legal asks specific credit formula tied to regional failure incidents.
- They want per-route latency SLOs (chat vs embeddings) and associated remedy. AE notes: "we can offer dedicated capacity SLOs but latency credits need legal signoff; propose staged language for POC -> SOW".

POC scope & acceptance criteria (agreed):
- 72h soak under realistic traffic (mix: 70% chat, 20% rerank, 10% embeddings).
- Failover drill #1: take eu-west-1 pool offline for 30 mins, verify us-east/ us-west absorb traffic with p95 latency degradation < 1.5x baseline.
- Failover drill #2: simultaneous region spike (2x) for 15 mins, verify fallback to quantized model keeps p99 within agreed delta.
- Quantitative targets: sustained 400 req/s per-region with p95 < 200ms; absorption to 800 req/s on failover with p95 < 350ms.

Open tech decisions / unknowns:
- Exact GPU SKU for Dedicated (customer prefers H100 but cost team weighing A100 80GB as compromise).
- KMS topology for cross-account key access - security team has follow-up questions.
- Network egress and data residency wording in contract needs infra signoff.

1) Run agreed POC (SE to provision POC pools w/ monitoring hooks).
2) Run failover drills and capture traces for SLO negotiation.
3) Draft Dedicated SOW with region-by-region capacity, failover headroom, and latency credit language for legal.
